facts.title: SpectrumKV: Per-Token Mixed-Precision KV Cache Transfer for Prefill-Decode Disaggregated LLM Serving
facts.event_hint: Reframes PD-disaggregated KV cache transfer as a per-token precision-allocation problem: high-importance tokens at FP16, medium at INT8, low at INT4, with a deployment-time probe to decide INT4 tolerance.
facts.problem: In prefill-decode (PD) disaggregated LLM serving, the KV cache becomes a network payload. Existing PD-side KV reduction methods are binary (full-precision-or-drop), which wastes a useful precision-allocation design space and can catastrophically damage quality on INT4-sensitive models.
facts.mechanism: Per-token mixed-precision KV transfer: attention sinks / high-importance tokens stay FP16; medium-importance tokens sent INT8; low-importance tokens sent INT4 when the model tolerates it. Because INT4 tolerance is model-dependent, SpectrumKV runs a lightweight deployment-time probe (three aggressive needle-in-a-haystack / NIAH trials under a 3-tier policy); models that pass use FP16+INT8+INT4, failing models fall back to FP16+INT8.

evidence.claim: At a 50% normalized KV budget on WikiText-2, SpectrumKV changes perplexity by +1.97%, -0.06%, and -0.44% on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Gemma-2-9B-it respectively, vs PDTrim's +25.85%, +22.07%, +35.63%.
On NIAH retrieval at 4096 tokens, the adaptive policy reaches 52.6% on Qwen at aggressive b=0.3 budget vs 26.3% for PDTrim, and reaches 100% by b=0.5.
End-to-end GPU timing of the transfer path shows 50-62% TTFT reductions at b=0.5.
Qwen2.5-7B catastrophically fails under INT4 KV quantization, while Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B remain stable.

facts.evaluation_context: Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Gemma-2-9B-it. Benchmarks: WikiText-2 perplexity, NIAH retrieval at 4096 tokens, end-to-end GPU transfer-path timing. Baseline: PDTrim (binary token selection).
facts.limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; full 28-page paper not fetched. Probe robustness on out-of-distribution workloads and absolute TTFT/network-byte numbers pending full-text validation. INT4 safety is model-dependent, so generalization beyond the three tested models is unverified.
facts.project_relevance: Highly relevant to the TPN / KVCache cross-node transfer track: it directly reduces the bytes shipped across the inference network per PD handoff while bounding quality loss, complementing network-side optimizations (NetKV, SmartGen). The precision-as-budget framing maps onto CXL/disaggregated-memory bandwidth allocation and onto DPU-offloaded KV compression, and it matters for agent serving where long context makes PD transfer bytes the dominant cost.
